title: Faith has six parts
hook: belief in Allah, His angels, books, messengers, the Last Day, and decree (Muslim)

segments.voice: Yesterday, fiqh close: the end of the long block on law. Your line: many roads, one direction.

The companions are sitting with the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ when a man walks in. His clothes are brilliantly white, his hair very black, and there's no dust of travel on him. Nobody in the room knows who he is. He sits knee to knee with the Prophet, rests his hands on his own thighs, and starts asking questions. What is islam? The Prophet answers, and the stranger says, you have spoken truly. The companions, as Umar tells it, were amazed that he asked and then confirmed the answer himself. Then the second question: tell me about iman.
screen: `A STRANGER IN WHITE.` → `KNEE TO KNEE.` → `TELL ME ABOUT IMAN.`

segments.voice: Day five met the word itself, from a root of safety and trust. Today, what it holds. This scene is in Sahih Muslim, and the answer is a list. Iman, the Prophet says, is to believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers and the Last Day, and to believe in the decree, its good and its harm. Six, and this week takes them one at a time. First, the shape of the conversation. The stranger asks three things in order. Islam is answered with things you do: the testimony, prayer, charity, fasting, pilgrimage. Iman is answered with things you hold true. Ihsan is answered with how you worship: as though you see Him, and if you don't see Him, knowing that He sees you. Body, belief and heart, in one sitting. Second, much of the list is already in the Qur'an. Pickthall's translation of one verse says of the believers: "Each one believeth in Allah and His angels and His scriptures and His messengers." The hadith gathers that together and adds the Last Day and the decree. Third, the stranger. After he leaves, the Prophet tells Umar it was Jibril, the angel Gabriel, come to teach the people their religion. An angel taught the list that includes the angels. Last, why a list. Six short items are easy to carry. A child can count them on one hand and one more finger; a scholar can spend a life on any one.
screen: `ISLAM, IMAN, IHSAN.` · `THE LIST IS IN THE QUR'AN TOO.` · `THE STRANGER WAS JIBRIL.` · then, large: `SIX TO CARRY.`

segments.voice: Hold up one hand and fold a finger down for each, slowly, aloud or in your head: Allah, the angels, the books, the messengers, the Last Day, and then the thumb of the other hand, the decree. Go through them once more, slower, and notice where your mind lingers; you don't have to say why.
Iman. Faith, belief: in the hadith of Jibril, belief in Allah, His angels, books, messengers, the Last Day, and the decree. Today's word.
Your line: six to believe. Tomorrow, the first of the six, and the shortest description of God. Peace until then.

howItsDone: The six articles of faith are taught as a list, and the hadith of Jibril is taught as a summary of the religion in three layers: islam, iman and ihsan.

chat.says: Muslims pray and fast, sure. But what do they actually believe?
options: Six things: Allah, His angels, books, messengers, the Last Day, and the decree.
Five things: the testimony, prayer, charity, fasting and the pilgrimage.
Just one thing: that God exists. The rest is up to each person.
